Makariv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kyiv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Makariv's cemetery held the grave of Menachem Nachum Twersky, founder of the Makariv branch of Chernobyl Hasidism in 1837, whose ohel has since been reconstructed by the organization Ohalei Tzaddikim — the same group responsible for restoring a Hasidic grave marker at Prybuzhany, elsewhere in this collection. The community itself, documented from the mid-18th century, grew rapidly through the 19th century to nearly 4,000 people by 1887, before Civil War-era violence in 1919 — led by warlords named Sokolovsky and Matviyenko — killed dozens and drove roughly 4,000 residents to flee. Nazi occupation in July 1941 brought the first recorded shooting of Jews anywhere in the Kyiv region; the cemetery itself was destroyed in the 1970s, with some tombstones relocated to Makariv's municipal cemetery.
